Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

wander verb

also wander about, wander around, roam, rove, ramble, stray, wandering

classical

Cic. Att. 8.9.3: circum vīllulās nostrās (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 13.821: multae quoque vallibus errant

errō, errāre, errāvī, errātum

verb, first conjugation

wander, stray, roam about

Going about with no fixed way or goal. It also, and very often, means to be wrong (see wrong); errāns is someone who has lost his way (quī errantī cōmiter mōnstrat viam, Enn. ap. Cic. Off. 1.51).

Other words

  • vagor, vagārī, vagātus sum — roam, range, stroll about

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.80: volucrēs hūc illūc passim vagantēs (Lewis & Short); Mart. 3.58.12

    Moving freely here and there, of people, flocks, birds, bees; the word for roaming at will rather than being lost.

  • pālor, pālārī, pālātus sum — straggle, wander about scattered

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Liv. 5.44: vagī per agrōs pālantur (Lewis & Short)

    Of a crowd or a herd that has scattered; mostly in the participle, pālantēs. Not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • vagātur omnis turba sordidae chortis, argūtus ānser gemmeīque pāvōnēs

    the whole grubby farmyard crowd wanders about, the honking goose and the jewelled peacocksMart. 3.58.12–13

  • hoc pecus omne meum est, multae quoque vallibus errant

    all this flock is mine, and many more are wandering in the valleysOv. M. 13.821

  • apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī, quae vagantur et flōrēs ad mel faciendum idōneōs carpunt

    we should copy the bees, as they say, which wander about and pick the flowers fit for making honeySen. Ep. 84.3

See also get lost, walk, wrong.
